page.layout: One printed page: a single text column, with a marginal note column on the right beside the upper part of the text. The left edge of the scan shows the neighbouring page, which is not transcribed.

main_text.p: piscopus Alexandrinus, qui huius Perse-quutionis pars magna fuit? bis ex Imperatoris Decreto in exilium relegatus, & indignissimè ab Arrianis tractus ad tribunalia, iniquissimè accusatus. Cur non imperij proceres ad imperatorem abdicandum hortatur? ægrè ferentes quòd in suos propinquos sæuiret, quòd Ablauio viro consulari & prætorij præfe-ctura decorato, mortem machinaretur. Et denique quòd illo si non iubente, si-nente saltem Dalmatius Cæsar, prosper-rima indole iuvenis (ut loquitur Eutro-pius) oppressus fuerit. Cur non popu-lum Alexandrinum numerosissimum sui præsulis obseruantissimum, & denique supra modum ad {n}seditionem à natura propensum, ad arma & tumultus concitet? Imò è contra, populo concitato, ut decebat tantum & talem Episcopum, pietate grauem,Epipha-nius hæresi 69. & Euag. lib.2.cap.8.

p.i: Ille regit dictis animos & pectora mulcet.

main_text.p: Et in Apologia sua ad Constantium illum Pijssimum & Religiosissimum, Augustum appellans, duobus criminibus Læsæ Majestatis sibi obiectis, in hunc modum dum

page.notes: The first word "piscopus" is a fragment carried over from the previous page; the initial "Epi" is cut off at the page edge. The "ct" in "pectora" is a ligature in the scan, read as "pectora". The reference mark "n" is printed as a superscript before "seditionem" and matches the margin note. The "?" after "concitet" and "fuit" are printed with a space before them. Long s is rendered as plain s throughout, including the "ff" ligatures in "indignissimè", "iniquissimè" and "Pijssimum". The line "Ille regit dictis..." is set as a separate verse line. The catchword "dum" and the signature "K 2" are printed at the foot of the page, not part of the text.
